surprises.body: Dobeš allowed 6 goals on 30 shots, worth 2.8 expected goals: 3.2 more than expected. Starting goalies have a night this rough about once every 45 starts.

story.head: The Penguins let a four-goal lead slip, then win it in overtime
paras: Cole Caufield struck first for the Canadiens early in the first, but Evgeni Malkin tied it 1-1 for Pittsburgh on the power play midway through the period. There were five goals in the second period alone. Declan Carlile scored his first goal for Pittsburgh just 32 seconds into the period to put the Penguins ahead 2-1. Samuel Girard made it 3-1 early in the period. Tommy Novak and Ben Kindel scored a minute and a half apart midway through the period to stretch the lead to 5-1. Nick Suzuki cut Pittsburgh’s lead to 5-2 a little over three minutes later, and Caufield struck again early in the third to make it 5-3. Pittsburgh had a goal taken off for offside early in the period, but it didn’t cost them in the end. With the goalie pulled and just over a minute left, Chris Kreider scored his first goal for Montréal to pull the Canadiens within one. With the goalie pulled and 44 seconds left, Ivan Demidov tied it up. Novak won it with his second goal of the night a minute and a half into overtime. Two players had three-point nights: Malkin with a goal and two assists, and Novak with two goals and an assist.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Artūrs Šilovs made 20 saves for the Penguins, and Jakub Dobeš allowed six goals on 30 shots. The Penguins improved to 2-0-0 with a win in their home opener, tied for first in the NHL in points percentage, while the Canadiens dropped to 1-0-1, giving up the best points percentage in the NHL to the Penguins.

items.text: Evgeni Malkin passed Dale Hawerchuk for 22nd on the NHL’s all-time scoring list, with 1,411 points.
Chris Kreider scored again against Pittsburgh, and has six goals in nine games against them since 2023-24.
One of the preview’s two calls held.
